title: MacBook Air 13-inch (M3)

evidence: Visible from outside.

components.label: Li-polymer battery (4 cells, 52.6 Wh)

components.function: Stores energy and powers the Mac when it is unplugged.

components.label: Stereo speakers (4-speaker system)

components.label: Logic board
evidence: A small board near the hinge; Apple's boards are far smaller than a PC motherboard.
Curated reference model of a typical MacBook Air 13-inch (M3) (standard teardown layout), not an AI scan of a photo.
components.function: Carries the M3 chip, storage and power circuits; every part plugs into it.

components.label: Apple M3 chip (CPU, GPU, Neural Engine)
evidence: Soldered to the logic board.

components.function: Runs macOS and every app; CPU, graphics and AI engine are on one chip.
components.ifRemoved: The Mac cannot start.

components.label: Unified memory (8–24 GB, on the chip package)
evidence: The memory chips sit next to the M3 on the same package, not in a slot.

components.function: Working memory shared by the CPU and GPU.
components.ifRemoved: The Mac cannot start; it cannot be replaced or upgraded.

components.label: SSD storage (NAND chips on the board)

components.function: Stores macOS, apps and files.
components.ifRemoved: Starts but finds nothing to boot from; the chips are soldered, not swappable.

components.label: Heat spreader (fanless cooling)

components.function: Spreads the M3's heat across the aluminium body; there is no fan.
components.ifRemoved: The chip heats up and slows itself down sooner.

summary: Apple's MacBook Air with the M3 chip: a fanless laptop whose small logic board carries the M3 with its unified memory and soldered SSD, powered by four flat battery cells under the palm rest; the Liquid Retina display hangs on one hinge in its own lid.
